sections.heading: Deeper means more pressure
sections.text:
Water has weight. The deeper you go, the more water there is above you pressing down, so the pressure increases with depth.
Fill a tin with water and make three holes at different heights: the jet from the lowest hole goes furthest.
Divers feel the pressure on their ears a few metres down; at the bottom of a deep lake it is very large.

sections.heading: Three more facts
sections.text:
• At a given depth the pressure acts equally in all directions: up, down and sideways.
• A denser liquid gives a larger pressure at the same depth (sea water more than fresh water).
• The shape of the container does not matter. A narrow pipe and a wide tank filled to the same depth have the same pressure at the bottom.
That is why dams, like those at Edéa and Song Loulou, are thickest at the bottom.

sections.heading: Calculating it
sections.text:
p = ρgh, with ρ the density in kg/m³, g = {10} N/kg and h the depth in metres.
At {5} m in water: p = {1000} × {10} × {5} = {50000} Pa.
This is the pressure due to the liquid. The air also presses on the surface, so the total pressure is atmospheric pressure + ρgh.

key_words.meaning: distance below the surface of the liquid
pressure due to a liquid column
a wall that holds back water

mistake.wrong: A wide tank has more pressure at the bottom than a narrow one of the same depth
mistake.right: The pressures are equal: only depth (and density) matter
mistake.why: p = ρgh has no area in it, so the width of the container does not matter.

cards.idea: Pressure increases with depth and acts in all directions.
example: Water squirts furthest from the lowest hole in a can.

cards.idea: The shape of the container does not matter, only the depth.
example: A wide and a narrow tank of the same depth have the same pressure at the bottom.

misconceptions.explain: Multiply by the depth h = {h} m too.

pick.q: A tin has three holes at different heights and is filled with water. Water squirts furthest from…
e: Near the top the depth, and so the pressure, is small.
Pressure increases with depth, so the jets differ.
pick.y: The deepest point has the greatest pressure.

pick.q: Why is a dam built thicker at the bottom than at the top?
w: Water is denser at the top
The top must hold more water
Pressure is greatest at the surface
e: The density is the same throughout.
Pressure is smallest at the surface.
pick.y: The wall must resist the large pressure near the bottom.

pick.q: At the same depth in a liquid, the pressure acts…
e: Liquid pressure also pushes sideways and upwards.
It also pushes down and up.
It also pushes down and sideways.
pick.y: Liquid pressure at a point is the same in every direction.
